design_reasoning.reason: Every architectural decision is grounded in either an existing ADR (ADR-003 skills-based architecture, ADR-004 sentinel/verify.sh contract, ADR-005/ADR-006 grader pattern, ADR-007 skill input independence) or a concrete pattern already present in the repo (the `devin` CLI subprocess pattern in evals/devin.js, the cadence-workflow-orchestration skill's documented local-quickstart and messaging/timer docs). The design is minimal: it does not reimplement skill logic, reuses the existing four SDLC skills unchanged, keeps the sentinel-file contract instead of inventing a parallel completion mechanism, and explicitly rejects unscoped additions (e.g., Slack/email notification) as out of scope. Where two layers touch the same concern (e.g., attempt counting), the design explicitly differentiates intent (Workflow owns durable in-process state vs. Repository owns persisted artifacts).
design_reasoning.recommendation: No changes required. Optionally add one line calling out why a generic `run_skill_activity(skill_name, ...)` Activity was preferred (or not) over four separate Activity functions, to remove the last bit of ambiguity between the two variants mentioned in the decision's impact field.

workflow_changes.reason: The happy path is fully specified as 9 sequential domain events, each naming the layers involved and the data flowing across handshake points (contract_used + data_shape), and it maps to the story's core acceptance criteria (end-to-end run, retry, escalation, auditability). The grade-repair loop and human-escalation-with-timeout are both modeled as explicit steps with recovery behavior (step 8 covers the timeout re-escalate-then-fail path). However, only 2 edge cases are modeled directly as workflow steps (loop exhaustion at step 5→7, and Signal timeout at step 8); the rubric's other story edge cases (Activity RetryPolicy exhaustion routing to escalation, oversized/empty/unicode input handling, duplicate concurrent WorkflowID rejection, worker-crash replay) are addressed only in architectural_decisions/questions_addressed rather than as explicit branches in workflow_sequence, so the happy-path model itself has fewer than the 4+ edge-case divergences the top score requires.
workflow_changes.recommendation: Add explicit workflow_sequence steps (or sub-branches on existing steps) for: (a) an Activity exhausting its own RetryPolicy and routing into HumanEscalationRaised with escalation_reason='activity_failure_exhausted_retries', and (b) the empty/oversized/duplicate-WorkflowID input validation that happens before step 2. This will make all of the story's edge cases traceable directly in the workflow model rather than only in the architectural decisions.

interface_contracts.reason: Five contracts are fully specified (WorkflowInput, GradeRepairLoopState, SkillActivityInterface, HumanEscalationSignal, CadenceClientInteraction), each with complete added/modified/removed shape definitions appropriate to a Cadence system (Signal/Query payload shapes and Activity input/output shapes in place of REST endpoints/status codes, which is the correct substitution for this domain). Every workflow_sequence handshake_point references one of these named contracts and a concrete data_shape, giving a clean 1:1 mapping between the workflow model and the contracts section.
interface_contracts.recommendation: No changes required. Consider adding the Activity-level error/failure shape (e.g., what fields an ActivityFailure carries back to the Workflow) to SkillActivityInterface to fully cover 'error handling' the way HTTP contracts would specify status codes.

layer_responsibilities.reason: All five layers (Client, Workflow, Activity, Cadence Service, Repository) have explicit new_responsibilities, each paired with an intent that ties back to the 'where is the information available to act' heuristic and to ADR-003's workflow/skill split. Responsibilities are consistent with existing architecture (skills keep authoring their own outputs; the Workflow only orchestrates; the Repository keeps the same file/sentinel shape) and no responsibility contradicts the audited current reality.

instrumentation.reason: Seven instrumentation events are defined (StartStoryAnalysisWorkflow, InvokeSkillActivity, CompleteSkillActivity, EvaluateGradeRepairLoop, RaiseHumanEscalationSignal, ReceiveHumanResponseSignal, CompleteStoryAnalysisWorkflow), each in VerbObject/VerbObjectContext form with 2-4 contextual data points, covering every major workflow branch (start, per-skill invocation/completion, loop decision, escalation raise/resolve, terminal completion) including error/timeout paths.
instrumentation.recommendation: No changes required. Consider adding a dedicated `RetryActivityAttempt` event distinct from CompleteSkillActivity so Cadence-managed Activity retries are visible in metrics/logs independent of the outer grade-repair attempt_count.
